title: Add SLO gate to automatically reduce/disable burst when non-burst latency regresses
author: Peter Holtz
release_notes: Reliability: burst capacity is now guarded by an automated SLO gate that reduces/halts burst allocations when non-burst tenants experience sustained tail-latency regression. Includes alert annotations and a rollback-safe feature flag.
description: Context: During burst beta we saw a small but meaningful class of incidents where a subset of non-burst tenants experienced elevated p95/p99 latency when a burst pool approached saturation (ref: SUP-28455 + internal beta notes). The existing global circuit breaker (pr-23919) protects the fleet when *burst pool* safety caps are exceeded, but it does not directly gate on the user-facing SLO impact we care about most: non-burst latency. This PR adds an SLO-based gate that automatically reduces or disables burst when neighbor (non-burst) latency regresses beyond configured thresholds for a sustained window. The gate is intentionally conservative and rollback-safe, with explicit hysteresis and auditability. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce BurstSloGate evaluator that consumes per-region/hardware SLO signals (non-burst p95/p99 latency + baseline) and emits a gating decision: ALLOW, REDUCE(max_burst_ratio=N), or DISABLE. (2) Wire gating decision into the burst admission controller so burst tokens/permits are capped or denied when gate is active; denial reasons are surfaced as `SLO_GATED` with details in debug endpoint. (3) Add configuration in policy engine for thresholds/windows/hysteresis (defaults are global; can be overridden by region/hardware allowlist for rollout). (4) Emit new metrics and annotate alerts so on-call can quickly see when/why the gate tripped and whether it is the dominant source of denials. Behavior (high level): - We compute `nonburst_tail_regression` as (current non-burst p95 latency / rolling baseline p95 latency) and similarly for p99. Baseline is a 30m EWMA excluding current 5m window to avoid self-inflation. - Gate enters REDUCE when regression exceeds threshold for `enter_window` (default 3m). In REDUCE we clamp effective `max_burst_ratio` (e.g., from 2.0 -> 1.2) and apply a minimum cooldown before reevaluating. - Gate enters DISABLE when regression exceeds a higher threshold OR when regression persists longer than `disable_after` (default 10m). DISABLE denies new burst permits immediately, but does not tear down existing in-flight requests. - Gate exits only after regression remains below `exit_threshold` for `exit_window` (default 10m) to avoid flapping. - Gate is scoped by region + hardware class (e.g., us-east/H100), and only enabled when `burst_slo_gate_enabled` flag is true and the region/hw is allowlisted. Non-goals: - This does not attempt to detect prompt-level or tenant-specific latency issues; it is a coarse safety mechanism. - This does not replace pool saturation circuit breaker; it complements it by keying off protected SLOs. Implementation notes: - SLO signal source: we reuse the existing latency histogram series aggregated by `tenant_class=dedicated_nonburst` (introduced in pr-23822 dashboards work) and compute regression in a lightweight evaluator in the admission controller process to avoid adding a new service dependency on the hot path. - Determinism: gating decision is computed on a fixed cadence (10s) and cached; admission requests within the cadence interval see the same gate decision. We also add smoothing + min-evaluation interval to reduce jitter under telemetry lag (aligns with hotfix approach in pr-23944). - Auditability: whenever the gate transitions state we emit an audit-style event to the internal event bus (not customer audit log) and add structured log fields (`gate_state`, `gate_reason`, `gate_metrics_snapshot`). - Observability: new Prometheus metrics include `burst_slo_gate_state{region,hardware}`, `burst_slo_gate_transitions_total{from,to,reason}`, and `burst_denials_total{reason="slo_gated"}`. Testing: - Unit tests for regression computation, hysteresis, and state transitions. - Integration test for admission controller: when gate=DISABLE, burst requests are denied with reason `SLO_GATED` and deterministic retry-after semantics are preserved. - Load test sanity: validated in staging with synthetic p95 inflation to ensure the gate trips and recovers without flapping. Rollout plan: - Behind feature flag + region/hardware allowlist (initially: us-east/H100 + eu-west/L40S staging only). - Once dashboards confirm sane behavior, we can enable for internal dogfood and then beta tenants. Operational notes: - On-call can manually override by disabling the flag or adjusting thresholds in config; both are logged and appear in debug output. - Alerts: add an alert when gate is DISABLE for >5m AND non-burst regression continues to worsen (indicates deeper issue than burst gating).
commits: admission: add BurstSloGate state machine + regression computation
policy: add config schema for slo gate thresholds/windows/hysteresis
admission: integrate gate decision into permit issuance + reason codes
obs: export slo gate metrics + alert annotations
tests: unit + integration tests for gating transitions and determinism
docs(internal): add runbook notes and links from alert to mitigation steps
conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): Can we guarantee we’re not keying off a metric that includes bursting tenants? We need this to be strictly non-burst class, otherwise we can create a feedback loop. Also, what’s the expected time-to-mitigate once non-burst p95 regresses?

Peter Holtz (author): Good call. The series used is `tenant_class=dedicated_nonburst` only; I added a guard that fails closed (DISABLE) if that label is missing/empty. Time-to-mitigate is enter_window (3m) + cadence (<=10s). For severe regressions we jump straight to DISABLE on the higher threshold.

Keiko Yamamoto (review): Please add a minimum clamp (e.g. don’t reduce below 1.0 unless DISABLE) and ensure cooldown won’t starve recovery. Also would like to see the default thresholds called out clearly.

Peter Holtz (author): Added `min_reduced_burst_ratio=1.0` invariant. Cooldown is now `min(2m, exit_window/2)` and we continue sampling during cooldown (we just don’t flip-flop states). Defaults documented in code + internal doc.

Jordan Lee (review): Determinism under telemetry lag: the evaluator running in-process could see partial scrapes. What happens if we miss a point? I’d prefer explicit stale detection and a stable cached decision, not jittering every 10s.

Peter Holtz (author): Implemented stale detection: if samples are older than 60s, gate transitions to REDUCE (not DISABLE) with reason `telemetry_stale` and keeps last good baseline. Admission path reads a cached decision updated on a ticker; it won’t change mid-request. Added tests for stale handling.

Mina Haddad (review): Routing behavior when `SLO_GATED`: should we treat it like capacity_exceeded and apply the same fallback policy? Also ensure the denial reason is surfaced to the router for logging.

Peter Holtz (author): Yes—router already treats burst denials similarly; I updated the mapping so `SLO_GATED` is categorized as non-retryable burst admission denial with existing fallback behavior (stick to baseline dedicated capacity). Also added `gate_state` to the structured denial payload consumed by routing logs/debug.

Allison Grant (review): Metric label cardinality: don’t add tenant labels. Region/hardware is fine, but please don’t add model. Also add an alert annotation that links to the overload mitigation runbook section specific to this gate.

Peter Holtz (author): Confirmed: metrics are region+hardware only, no tenant/model labels. Added alert annotations and a short internal doc section; also linked the alert to the existing burst pool overload runbook with a new subsection for SLO gate.
Sean Gallagher (final): Looks good. Please ensure we have a manual kill switch documented and that the alert doesn’t page during planned load tests.

Peter Holtz (author): Kill switch is `burst_slo_gate_enabled=false` (feature flag) and `burst_slo_gate_allowlist=[]` to hard-disable. Alert is warning by default; paging only when DISABLE > 15m and non-burst regression persists. Updated alert routing notes.
